hints: Notice the arrow lengths on the top face, bottom face and at different heights on the left and right faces.
Recall liquid pressure increases with depth as $p = h\rho g$ and the force on an area is $F = pA$ acting perpendicular into the block.
Check which diagram has left-right symmetry at each level, larger arrows deeper down, and larger upward arrows than downward arrows.
walkthrough: Identify the rule: liquid pressure depends on depth, $p = h\rho g$, so deeper liquid pushes harder on the same area.
Apply to top and bottom: the force is $F = pA$ normal to the surface, so the upward arrows on the deeper bottom face must be longer than the downward arrows on the shallower top face.
Apply to the sides: at any one horizontal level the depth $h$ is the same left and right, so the inward horizontal arrows must be equal in length on both sides.
Apply down the sides: $h$ increases downward, so the inward side arrows must get progressively longer toward the bottom.
Only one diagram shows symmetric side forces growing with depth together with bottom forces larger than top forces. This is option A.

options.A: Side arrows are equal left-right at each depth and grow longer with depth, while bottom arrows are longer than top arrows, matching $p = h\rho g$.
options.B: It shows no horizontal forces on the sides, but liquid pressure acts normal to all submerged faces.
options.C: The upper side arrows point outward and are not symmetric in length with depth, which pressure cannot produce.
options.D: The side arrows have equal length at all depths, but pressure must increase with depth so lower forces must be larger.
